subject.title: Add external event hooks for quota and provider state changes

question: Should CodexBar accept opt-in execution of user-configured local commands, together with the proposed stable hook config, event, payload, and CLI contract, after the argument editor is made lossless?
rationale: The patch can be mechanically corrected, but tests cannot decide whether a quota observer should become a general local automation launcher or whether the project wants to support this security-sensitive external contract long term.

options.title: Accept after lossless editor fix
options.body: Preserve argv exactly, retain the direct-exec/environment/redaction safeguards, add upgrade-contract coverage, and then land the feature as an explicitly supported opt-in surface.

options.title: Narrow the surface first
options.body: Keep the core event model but reduce or redesign the UI, CLI, or config contract before committing to a broad public automation API.

options.title: Decline local command hooks
options.body: Close the paired feature direction and keep CodexBar limited to observability and existing notification or serve-based integration surfaces.

recommendation.title: Accept after lossless editor fix
recommendation.body: Preserve argv exactly, retain the direct-exec/environment/redaction safeguards, add upgrade-contract coverage, and then land the feature as an explicitly supported opt-in surface.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a repository-wide product and security boundary rather than an isolated implementation choice.
